## My Pick: **Polis** (Project #6)

Polis is the single project that most completely embodies my values across every dimension I weight most heavily. It is genuinely open source, cooperatively stewarded, and has proven civic infrastructure value through deployment in vTaiwan's democratic processes and EU consultations — demonstrating that AI-assisted deliberation can serve democratic legitimacy rather than undermine it. Critically, it sits at the exact intersection of my active research concerns: it is simultaneously an AI governance tool *and* an AI-powered civic tool, meaning it models the kind of transparent, accountable AI application I argue for professionally while generating real governance insights about how AI shapes public deliberation. Its community governance structure and the concrete evidence of state-level adoption without commercial capture make it meaningfully different from participation-washing projects, and its low-barrier open deployment model genuinely empowers under-resourced civic technologists globally.

---

**Close runners-up I want to acknowledge:** Decidim was genuinely difficult to pass over — its cooperative governance and scale are extraordinary — and the *Principles for Public Participation in AI Procurement* (#9) speaks most directly to my AI governance research. But Polis uniquely unites the builder and critic roles in one living, proven system.
